title: A JSON response from a template

blocks.text: The page's first use case is a JSON response body: a text block holds the template, and `formatted()` fills it. The page also warns that `formatted()` does no escaping of its own.
Write `ApiResponse.json(int status, String message, String data)`. It returns these five lines joined by `\n`, with no newline after the last:

items: `data` is already JSON (an array, an object, `null`) and goes in as it is.
`message` is a JSON string: a backslash in it is written `\\` and a double quote `\"`. Escape the backslashes before the quotes.
The values are **arguments** to `formatted()`, never part of the template, so a `%` in the message is printed as it is.

cases.says: The status, the message and the raw data fill the five-line JSON template, with no newline at the end.
A double quote in the message is written \" so the JSON string stays closed.
A backslash in the message is written \\, and escaping it first keeps a quote's escape from being doubled.
A % in the message is printed as it is, never read as a format specifier.

concepts: formatted() inserts values as they are, so each value is escaped for its format, and values go in as arguments, never into the template.
A text block holds a JSON body with its quotes unescaped, and formatted() fills in the values.
